name: Hawk & Hawthorne
title: Hawk & Hawthorne Wedding DJ & Host | Dan's Events
description: Planning a wedding at Hawk & Hawthorne in Barnardsville, NC? See Ritual Hill, the Heritage Barn and the Heart Spring, plus my sound and lighting plan.
h1: Hosting, DJ and lighting at Hawk & Hawthorne
lede: Hawk & Hawthorne is fifty acres at the edge of Pisgah National Forest in Barnardsville, with a standing-stone ceremony hill, a tobacco barn and a heart-shaped spring. It is a working land sanctuary, and the sound and power need planning.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Barnardsville, NC, near Asheville, on 50 acres at the edge of Pisgah National Forest. No street address is published; visits are by appointment, registration or ticketed event only.

facts.label: Spaces
facts.value: Ritual Hill (outdoor ceremony), the Heritage Barn (a renovated tobacco barn used for dinner, dancing and as a rainy-day backup) and the Heart Spring.

facts.label: Time on site
facts.value: Five hours of prep the day before, then full-day access from 9 a.m. to midnight on the wedding day.

facts.label: Sound and music
facts.value: The venue says concert-grade sound equipment is provided, and lists live musicians, DJs and dance bands through its network.

facts.label: Scale
facts.value: The venue says it hosts only 10 to 15 weddings a year.

sections.h2: Fifty acres and three places to gather
p: Ritual Hill is an open sanctuary framed by standing stones and mountain views, used for ceremonies. The Heritage Barn is a renovated tobacco barn above a flower farm, used for dinner, the dance floor and as the rainy-day backup. The Heart Spring is a heart-shaped spring beside a hawthorn tree, suggested for performances and small gatherings that bring water into the celebration.
The home page also mentions a tobacco barn turned into a listening room and a cedar stage on Ritual Hill, which tells me the place is built for performance.

sections.h2: Sound and hosting on the land
p: The venue says it provides concert-grade sound equipment and connects couples with live musicians, DJs and high-energy dance bands. That means my first question is how outside entertainers fit, because I may be working with the venue's sound, not instead of it. If you want me hosting and running music, I would ask what is included in the venue's sound set and plan around it.

Open hillside ceremonies are an outdoor sound job with wind and no walls, so I use a close mic for the officiant and put the speakers near the front rows. Moving guests from Ritual Hill to the barn is a walk, so I host that transition with a short announcement and music. With access from 9 a.m. to midnight, there is room for a long, unhurried timeline.

Dusk is the point of this place: the valley, the barn lights and the ridge. I keep lighting warm and low, with wash lights on the barn beams and a spotlight for the entrance and first dance. On Ritual Hill I light the couple and the stones and leave the sky alone.

Low fog needs its own dedicated 30 amp circuit because it draws up to 3,000 watts for about five minutes at warm-up. Lights and sound run on 20 amp circuits. On a farm site with a barn and a hill, cable runs can be long, so I ask where the power is and send a plan. The venue mentions fire-circle gatherings but does not publish a sparkler, fog or open flame rule, so I get cold sparks and fog approved in writing.

Visits are by appointment, registration or ticketed event only, so book a tour rather than driving up. Weekday, off-season and micro weddings are priced differently from peak weekends, and the venue says it hosts micro weddings and elopements.

The venue lists five hours of prep the day before, which is a good time for a sound check. It says housing for the family and five-star accommodations are available on the land. It does not publish a capacity or a music cutoff, so ask both.

faq.a: It is in Barnardsville, NC, north of Asheville at the edge of Pisgah National Forest. The venue describes itself as near Asheville and does not publish a street address.

faq.q: Can I bring my own DJ and host?
faq.a: The venue provides concert-grade sound equipment and connects couples with its own musicians. I would ask whether an outside DJ and host can work with that setup before you sign.
The venue does not publish one. Full-day access ends at midnight, so ask your coordinator what the music limit is on your date.

faq.q: Can we use cold sparks or fog?
faq.a: The venue does not publish a rule on either. I ask for written approval for your date before planning the effect.
